newsitem.title: USA: No sign of inflationary pressures now, Yellen says.
newsitem.headline: No sign of inflationary pressures now, Yellen says.

text.p: White House chief economist Janet Yellen said on Monday she saw no sign of mounting inflationary pressures now.
"There is no evidence at this point of inflationary pressure," she told a luncheon meeting sponsored by the Center for National Policy.
Yellen said that workers' wages have picked up recently, but she argued that what was important was overall employment compensation, including benefits such as health care.

"Compensation growth has virtually been flat as a pancake for some time ... at about three percent," she said. "That is not a level of compensation growth that is worrisome at all from an inflation point of view."
Yellen, a former Federal Reserve Governor, steered clear of commenting directly on the central bank's policies, saying she respected its independence.
She did though say that she supported in principle the Fed's policy of acting pre-emptively against inflation, noting the long lags with which interest rates affect the economy.
However, she tempered that support by pointing to what she called "the great deal of uncertainty" now about how the economy is operating, including the level of full employment.
